I would like to show it to you again in order to show you yet another document, and what I can see in the document is an order where a distinction is made between two categories of persons or individuals: Those who are not under any suspicion that they committed a disciplinary breach, and those for whom there is reasonable doubt to suspect -- or reasonable suspicion that they committed a breach of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The basis for this order is Article 6, paragraph 1, of the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia, at least that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a list mentioned as the basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to us stay in private session, although this is a public document, but I would like us to stay in private session just for a moment to remind the Trial Chamber of the contents of Article 6. I would like to call document number P197, page 2 in B/C/S, please, as well as in English, I believe. We will look at the basis for issuing the previously shown order. It says: "In order to implement documents issued by the president of the Republic and the duties of a commanding in the army" -- yes I'm reading too fast. Article says as follows: "In order to implement documents issued by the president of the Republic and the duties of commanding the army, as well as the duties stipulated by this Law, the chief of General Staff shall issue rules, orders, commands, instructions, and other documents." This would be the basis of the documents that I showed you previously. And now let us look at the document P708, under seal. Kindly read the document slowly, Mr. Starcevic. I don't think you've had an opportunity to see it or read it before. It is a two-page long document. Read it slowly. Alert us at the moment when you have reached the end of the first page. We'll move on to the next then. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Counsel, when you speak next time, please -- you're asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, first of all, the date. 30 August 1995 is the date on this document. And these are the minutes of the 43rd Session of the Supreme Defence Council which was held in August 1995. The document was signed by President Zoran Lilic. The first thing that is stated on page 1 of this document is this: Mr. Lilic says the RSK defence ceased to exist, so the Supreme Defence Council concludes that there is no longer grounds to keep on assisting the armed forces of the RSK. Let's put things in temporal context. This is after Operation Storm and after the exodus of the Serbian population at the beginning of August 1995; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council, pursuant, and on the basis of certain facts reaches a conclusion to the effect that the Serbian Army of Krajina had ceased to exist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This would be exactly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't see the first page. And there's testimony about the first page of this document, and the English version on the screen is the second page. I merely ask that the first page be displayed while we're having questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I need page 2 in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking for something. Can you repeat the request, please, the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreting Mr. Lukic's words. Mr. Lukic is asking for page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What the Supreme Defence Council concludes in paragraphs 1, 2, and 3, is the fact that there is a difference between the two categories of the members of the 40th Personnel Centre, those who committed a disciplinary or a criminal act, and those who didn't, or, rather, there is no suspicion that they did; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 4, it says that those for whom there is no suspicion can selectively be assigned to a -- the units of the RSK or to the 30th Personnel Centre. Do you agree that these conclusions of the Supreme Defence Council are the basis based on which Mr. Perisic issued his order in view of the -- these conclusions and in view of the contents of that order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. This is just repetition of the conclusions that we see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we can go back to open session, and we can try to achieve something in this courtroom with the help of the other party to the proceedings. Can we now please see 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was waiting for the interpretation. I must now move us into open session as you asked. May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 8815 is the document that I would like to call.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To this document, Your Honour, Mr. Lukic is calling up is the English translation of the previous document that he had -- for which we had not identified an English translation existing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh. This is not an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So we do have it now. And what is on the right-hand side? That's -- on right-hand side, we don't have the document that we didn't have a translation for. It is some other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's one and the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are going back to it [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm going back. Just a small correction before that, correction in the transcript on page 75 line 15, the answer starts but it has been attached to the question. The witness said I agree. This is the beginning of the witness's answer. It is not part of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down a little to see the date -- no, no, no. This is how we're going do it. This is it an order on establishing the responsibilities and powers of officers regarding service-related issues in the Yugoslav Army. This is the order that you have already testified about. In very general terms, you have referred to the order on responsibilities and this is the document that had in mind every time you did that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to page 3 in B/C/S to see who issued the order. I suppose that the page will be the same in the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The order was issued by the chief, Colonel-General Momcilo Perisic, on the 25th April, 1994, and it was published in the official military gazette on the 5th of May, 1994, as you can see in the upper left corner. Mr. Starcevic, I don't know how to proceed. The document has three pages. Do you want to look at everything or maybe I could proceed in the following way: I could ask you this and do things in this way. In this document, this order has eight bullet points or articles in which it specifies certain categories of units and institutions and then in subparagraphs it gives them certain responsibilities and powers. Let's go back. It was very difficult for me to follow the numbers, but let's go back to page number 1. And let me look at the English translation, if I may, at the same time. Yes. Under number 1 -- no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, what I'm looking at is the book of rules on education.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Under number 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, could the usher please make sure that Mr. Starcevic is looking at the correct document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct now. We have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's read about the first category. It says: "The commander of an independent battalion or division and the commanding officer of an independent military unit or military institute with establishment rank of major, lieutenant-colonel, or higher, is authorised to ..." And then he is authorised according to certain bullet points, the last being number 3. These are the responsibilities arising from service. I'm not going to read everything, but what they deal with is appointment, dismissal, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the general approach from a lower unit to a higher unit, from a lower rank to a higher rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The following category is under number 2. Again, bullet points under number 2, pertaining to that rank, unit, or institution. And then the following page, please. Number 3, I don't want to keep on reading, you can see that the order that is followed is from the lowest ranking to the highest ranking -- or, rather, I would kindly ask for page -- for the following page in B/C/S to be placed on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the lower part of that page, where we see number 7, the right-hand side column. Under number 7, we arrive at the chief of General Staff, personnel administration is hereby authorised to do whatever he is given to do as specified in the following bullet points; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the following page in both English and B/C/S versions. Can we scroll up the page just a little, please. And after number 17, there's bullet-point 8, which I would like to zoom in on, after number 17, that's the 17th responsibility pertaining to the previous category. And then we come to number 8, the highest category and its responsibilities and powers. And it says here: "This is the assistant chiefs of General Staff, chief (at the same time chief inspector) of the chief army inspectorate, chief of the General Staff Security Administration, and chief of the General Staff information and psychological propaganda administration are authorised to executed duties ..." and then it says from item 5, paragraph 1. Can you please look at that. And what I would like to repeat is what I asked you previously, has to do with the following article, Article 10. The following articles apply to all the collective articles to put it that way, Article 10. Pursuant to Article 10, all the authorisations from items 1 through 8 include procedures which precedes the processing or issuing of the relevant enactments; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This order clearly and precisely determines the responsibilities of all personnel in the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the status in the service. In my last question, let us be more precise. My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This order clearly and precisely determines responsibilities for resolving the status of all personnel in the Yugoslav Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it provides in a precise terms who makes decisions about certain categories with respect to their position and rank.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to offer this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to go back again to the prior -- to a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have document P2424 under seal, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've seen this personnel chart of one of the officers. I'm putting this on the screen just to lead us to the next document. It says here that on the 9th of May, 1995, the professional service was terminated, due to five days of leave of absence from work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document P2425, MFI, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please speak into his microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You saw this document yesterday as well, where it says that this is a document issued by the Drina Corps command. You will remember when we scrolled the document down that this document was issued by the Army of Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was signed by Radislav Krstic. It bears the stamp of the Army of Republika Srpska, and in the -- in the bottom left corner you have an incoming stamp which means this is the stamp of the recipient; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that is the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Now in the statement of reason, the second sentence reads that it has been established that the above-named will not return to the unit which he wilfully abandoned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Without interpreting the meaning of this, can we please scroll down the document, and I would ask you for another comment. There are some notes made by hand, and I noticed that the English translation does correspond to what is written in the Serbian language, so I'm going to read it out to you and then ask for your opinion. It says, handwritten, wait for the reply from the GS Main Staff of the 30th Personnel Centre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then beneath, it says submitted the request for PPVS. I'm asking you what does this PPVS stand for; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very unusual acronym. I can only try to -- to decipher it. I believe that it might mean early termination of military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any case, it says that an individual has submitted a request for PPVS, and in that term, it seems that it was not translated properly into English, because I don't think that it tallies with what this acronym might mean. Therefore, this what is provided by the translation unit doesn't stand to reason. Anyway I'm going to ask the witness again. In the English translation, it says that PPVS means recognition of the entitlement for double length of service.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hardly understand this to mean that. I don't even understand what it means in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think the record should be clear -- I mean, that's not an assertion, there's a question mark before that. The translation that is offered on this exhibit has a question mark. There is no certainty that that's what the interpreter intended or the translator intended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What then do we do with this exhibit? I see it's an exhibit. It is not marked for identification. Shall we mark it for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I suggested earlier about some documents, simply what appears in the documents as acronyms shouldn't be expanded and should -- this expansion should be disregarded because the original documents contain only acronyms. I am in favour of sending this back to the translation unit, but I don't think we should burden them with a request that was provided only as a comment from the translation unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told it is marked for identification already any way. But I do think in response to what you are saying, sir, if we are now going to put acronyms only in the English version without telling -- expanding them, then we are lost. So we want a full -- a full translation. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think the proper way to deal with this particular expansion would be to disregard the translator's question mark, recognition of entitlement for double length of service, and leave it at that. Because neither Mr. Starcevic knows what that expansion means, nor did the language assistants who translated that, so obviously the proper way to do this is just disregard this particular expansion for the purposes of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that is the best solution. At any rate, the acronym PPVS could mean that the individual has submitted a request for --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I object to that. That's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can take the oath and take over. [Overlapping speakers] ... [Microphone not activated] You are now testifying on that issue that we have not been able to resolve.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hmm. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we suppose, Mr. Starcevic, that a certain individual decides to leave the Army of Republika Srpska and does not join the Yugoslav Army, is this individual eligible for receiving the salary and/or other benefits and fringe benefits due to him or should all the payments be suspended?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If, on the basis of all the enactments of the Yugoslav Army, he is appointed to a certain position including in the Army of Republika Srpska - I'm not going into the issue of whether that was legal or illegal - then that creates a basis for his receiving all the payments and fringe benefits. If he is not carrying out his duties, then he cannot receive the -- the pay and the fringe benefits. However, a declaratory act or a document has to be issued in which the fact shall be stated that he has abandoned his duty and that he was not discharging the duties for which he had been assigned to a certain post.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look now at document P2420, MFI. Mr. Harmon asked you some questions about this document too. You saw this document yesterday, and you will remember that we decided that this was a judgement of the Military Disciplinary Court of the Army of the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We spoke about the second co-accused. We see his personal details here, Nedeljko Vujic, a major from VP 7272, Banja Luka, then there are some other personal details. And then it says currently residing at an unknown address, a Serb, joined the VRS on the 4th of March, 1993. This judgement was rendered on 20th September, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear that he joined on the 4th of March, 1993. Okay, now we've got the relevant date. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in the judgement rendered on the 20th of September, 1995, the court established that the major's address is unknown? Let us now look at document 2421, under seal, another document that you saw yesterday. If you remember, you saw a document admitted by Ljubisa Velickovic yesterday, and you said that this is a document by the command of the anti-aircraft defence of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the date is 29 January, 1996. Under number 1, you see a reference to Nedeljko Vujic, who now holds the rank of lieutenant-colonel in the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I find interesting - can the document be scrolled up - is what Mr. Velickovic says in this document that he writes to the command of the air force and anti-aircraft defence. Says here that officer under number 1, i.e., Nedeljko Vujic, and under number 4, are serving in the Army of Yugoslavia and have been serving there for other two years and are achieving very good and excellent results. So a possible confirmation of this measure would be a pure loss for the RV and PVO of the VJ. From this document it arises, and I am sure you will agree with me, that this person, Nedeljko Vujic, who according to the previous judgement was residing in an unknown place in May, was serving in the VJ all that time, and he was even promoted. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how it looks, according to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just let's clear something up. Did I not hear that the previous document judgement was rendered on the 20th of September, 1995. And this one is dated ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] January 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 29 January 1996. And in January 1996, they're saying he has been in the VJ for two years, which goes beyond 20th -- yeah, okay. [Microphone not activated] you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at another document that Mr. Harmon showed you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P2422, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let's bring this Vujic story to an end. On the 12th of October, 2005, his professional military service was discontinued. He held the rank of colonel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the reason for termination was his 30 years of seniority or active military service?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 30 years of active military service and his service was discontinued.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this mean or would you agree with me that the Army of Yugoslavia, when this person fled from the Army of Republika Srpska, and pursuant to the previous document, joined the Army of Yugoslavia, and was there all that time, did not want to act on the decision of the Army of Republika Srpska, because he remained in the VJ until he was pensioned off and he was even promoted. He went up through the ranks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you know that the reason for him leaving was because he did not want to serve in the Army of Republika Srpska? I don't know the reason why he left. How do you know the reason he left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, and I have never mentioned any reasons. I'm just mentioning facts. Mr. Lukic asked me whether this mean that the Army of Yugoslavia did not want to accept the decision of the Army of Republika Srpska with regard to this person, Vujic. And my answer to that was yes, the Army of Yugoslavia did not accept that particular decision. Why he had left, why the army did not accept the decision, I never spoke about that because I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I misheard -- sorry, I misheard your question. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. All I want is to clarify this. Pursuant to the decision of the Military Disciplinary Court, which is document P2420, pursuant to that decision issued by the Army of Republika Srpska, it was established that he was a deserter from the Army of Republika Srpska; and that this happened on the 20th of May, 1993, at least according to the judgement. Could we call it a day, Your Honours, at this moment, but let's, before that, go into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I just want to read the transcript and clarify one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic says that it was established that he was a deserter from the army, and this happened on the 20th of May, 1993. First of all, I'm not sure what Mr. Lukic is referring to when he says it was established he was a desert on 20 May 1993. I don't think that accurately states the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I read this, and we have to go back into private session for me to answer this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decision of the Military Disciplinary Court, number P2420, MFI, in the statement of reasons, it says on page 1, on the 20th of May, 1993, Nedeljko Vujic, and before that he said that he wilfully, without the knowledge and approval by the superior organs, left his post and duty. This is what the court established and put on paper on the first page of its judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't have this on the [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says in the decision they are guilty. The numbers is 2420. If we can bring the document back on the screen, you will see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I want to correct, Your Honour. What the English translation that I have says that Mr. Vujic absconded from his unit on 29th of May, 1993. The record reflects the 20th in the transcript, the 20th of May, 1993. I was merely trying to correct what -- an error --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You agree the 29th, not the 20th because we don't have the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the original, I read 20 May, 1993. Can you see it in the B/C/S version. It may be a mistake in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which paragraph in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the three paragraph under different numbers, where particulars are provided for the individual, it says they are guilty. And then in the middle, if you are following, it says Nedeljko Vujic on 20th of May, 1993. Your Honours, this is in B/C/S line 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to just tell us where to look at on the screen, sir? Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the middle of the screen after the words "are guilty."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in B/C/S, it is "Krivisu," underneath that, line 5, you will see it says, Vujic, Nedeljko, and what follows is the date, 20th of May, in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in English, it says 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We will get that remedied, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We'll resubmit this and -- we can either do it one of two ways, Your Honour. We can either resubmit this English translation and get it corrected, or we could correct it now orally on the record and just note that this date is wrong and be satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And which date shall we go by?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would insert -- I think both parties agree we would insert the corrected date from the original, which would be 20 May, 1993, instead of 29 May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine it is so corrected. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We -- Mr. Starcevic, the usual warning. You don't discuss while you are still in the witness stand. The matter stands adjourn to tomorrow, tomorrow the 11th of June, at quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of June, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
